historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: mid-cycle blend of online music (+23% 5yr CAGR, 81% of revenue, decelerating toward low double digits) and social entertainment (-21% 5yr CAGR, 19% of revenue), plus Ximalaya consolidation in FY2026-27; equity CAGR is distorted by the FY2025 one-off gain and FVOCI revaluations, EPS CAGR by the same gain
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 18.6% and EPS 3yr CAGR 46.1% diverge >30% from revenue 3yr CAGR 5.1%: FY2025 EPS carries the RMB2,373m deemed-disposal gain (ex-gain EPS ~RMB2.85, 3yr CAGR ~36%), and shareholders' equity carries FVOCI revaluation gains that never pass through earnings. Owner-FCF (SBC and interest stripped) 3yr CAGR 7.4% vs reported 9.1%: the gap is interest income growing with the cash pile (711 -> 1,054), not SBC, which has been flat at ~RMB650m.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on FY2020-FY2025 (5yr) and FY2022-FY2025 (3yr). Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income; lease cash not deducted historically for lack of the full 5-year series): FY2020 3,193; FY2021 2,808; FY2022 5,578; FY2023 5,015; FY2024 7,451; FY2025 7,320. Equity series starts FY2021 (50,317), so only a 4yr CAGR (12.4%) exists on the normalized view.

scenario_narratives.base: Online music keeps compounding on monetisation rather than users: the paying ratio (22.9% in FY2025, from 17.1% in FY2023) and ARPPU (RMB11.8) keep rising at a slowing pace while MAUs drift lower, so music revenue grows ~11% in FY2026 fading to mid-single digits; social entertainment keeps shrinking 5-8% a year under live-streaming compliance limits until it is a rump. Ximalaya consolidates ~RMB7bn of revenue at a mid-teens margin, diluting the blended EBITDA margin to 33.5% in FY2027 before the music mix shift and content-cost leverage take it to 36%. The reported US$1bn buyback and the ~33% dividend increase continue; the share count is held flat and SBC (2% of revenue) is expensed. Terminal growth 2.5% nominal RMB, Gordon at 10.5%, capped at 18x.
scenario_narratives.bull: SVIP/membership tiers, ad-supported tiers, offline shows and artist merchandise push music ARPPU and paying ratio further than the Street expects; Ximalaya cross-sell adds a long-form audio subscription layer to 127m music payers and its margin converges toward the group's; AI product features arrest the MAU decline. Revenue grows 19%/15% in FY2026-27 (organic ~8%) and holds high single digits through year 5; blended EBITDA margin reaches 40% by year 8 as content costs scale and social entertainment stabilises as a small, compliant business. Terminal growth 3.0%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The path the current price implies after the 63% drawdown from the 52-week high: ByteDance's Soda Music and Douyin keep taking music discovery and listening time, so MAU decline spreads into paying-user decline from FY2028 and ARPPU growth stalls under the SAMR fee-cap conditions; social entertainment is regulated down further; Ximalaya is integrated at a loss with goodwill impairment, and content royalty escalation on label renewals compresses the blended EBITDA margin to 25%. Revenue grows only on the Ximalaya consolidation then declines 2-3% a year before flattening; terminal growth 1.0% with a 12x cap. The cash pile, term deposits and the FVOCI portfolio remain the floor under the equity.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the operating platform on fully-normalised owner FCF -- SBC expensed, interest and investment income stripped, FY2025's RMB2.4bn deemed-disposal gain removed, leases charged once, NCI charged once -- at an RMB-built 10.5% discount rate, then add the balance-sheet assets whose income was stripped: RMB34.5bn of net cash and term deposits (less a 5% repatriation friction and the RMB9bn Ximalaya cash paid after year-end) and the RMB27.9bn investment portfolio at a 25% haircut. The 10-year horizon lets the Ximalaya margin dilution wash through before capitalising. The 15% hurdle entry prices and the required-return table show what the HK$34 price implies; at this price most of the market capitalisation is covered by cash, deposits and investments, so the finding is about whether the music-subscription franchise is in structural decline (bear) or merely slowing (base).
key_risks_to_valuation: Online music ARPPU/paying-ratio growth stalls under SAMR fee-cap conditions while MAUs keep declining to ByteDance's Soda Music -- the bear growth path
Label royalty escalation or non-renewal (minimum guarantees) compressing gross margin; MCSC agreements only partly cover composition rights
Ximalaya integration: goodwill (~RMB9.2bn) impairment, margin dilution persisting beyond FY2027, no-exclusivity and free-content remedies limiting synergy
Further live-streaming/virtual-gifting regulation accelerating the social entertainment decline
China discount rate and VIE/WVR governance: a 1pp move in WACC is worth more per share than any single operating driver (see sensitivity grid); Tencent's 93.6% voting control
Investment portfolio (FVOCI RMB26.2bn, listed stakes marked to market) and trapped-cash/withholding-tax friction on the RMB38bn gross cash -- the bridge is ~45% of the house equity value
RMB/HKD translation: all per-share values are converted at a dated rate; refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate
Share count: the reported Q2-2026 US$400m ADS buyback is not taken (count deliberately high); the Ximalaya founder tranche is included before issuance

inputs.share_count_basis: 3,147.809m ordinary shares outstanding at 2026-03-31 (FY2025 20-F cover note, 1,482.9m Class A + 1,664.9m Class B) + 41.548m dilutive options/RSUs (FY2025 treasury-stock-method table, note 11) + 153.8m Class A shares issued to Ximalaya sellers at the May-2026 closing (5.1986% tranche) + ~11.6m founder tranche (0.37%) still to be issued at the first anniversary = 3,354.8m. Held FLAT thereafter because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). The reported ~US$400m of ADS repurchases in Q2-2026 would REDUCE this count by roughly 80-90m shares but is third-party reporting, not a filing, so it is not taken: the count is deliberately on the high side. Non-SBC issuance (Ximalaya acquisition currency) is modelled explicitly in the count, not via annual_share_growth_pct.
inputs.net_debt_note: Balance sheet 2025-12-31 (FY2025 20-F, RMB'million): cash and cash equivalents 8,470 + term deposits with initial terms over three months 29,573 (current 13,810 + non-current 15,763; cash-flow statement and note 21(a)) = 38,043 gross; less notes payable 3,497 (US$500m 2.000% senior notes due 2030; the 2025 tranche of 2,131 was repaid in FY2025). Short-term investments were ~nil at year-end (3,800 placed, 3,851 received). Lease liabilities (200 non-current + 116 current = 316) are EXCLUDED because leases are charged inside the flows (treatment B). Repatriation friction and the post-balance-sheet Ximalaya cash consideration are itemised in equity_bridge rather than netted here so a reader can flex each.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F cash-flow note 29(a), 'Non-cash employee benefits expense - share based payments' RMB669m (FY2024 596, FY2023 649). The company publishes no combined SBC-plus-equity-award-tax figure and the KPI EquityAwardTaxes is 0; the RMB281m 'Shares withheld for share award schemes' in financing is market purchases of shares to settle awards, i.e. the buyback-type mechanism that funds the flat count, so it is counted under buyback_cash and NOT added to SBC.
inputs.last_fcf_note: owner FCF = reported FCF 9,043 (OCF 10,231 - PPE 305 - intangibles 883) - SBC 669 - interest income 1,054 (income-statement figure; interest received in OCF was 1,240) - lease cash 135 (principal 124 in financing + ~11 lease interest) = 7,185. FY2025 OCF carried an unusual working-capital OUTFLOW of 1,033 (accounts payable -783, other operating assets -416); the component build at the recorded drivers gives a normalised FY0 owner FCF of ~8,300 (25% of revenue), so FY0 is a trough-WC year, not a run-rate.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflows: repurchase of ordinary shares 390 + shares withheld for share award schemes 281 = 671, against SBC of 669 -- the flat count was fully funded in cash in FY2025. Prior years: FY2024 1,925+217, FY2023 1,249+100, FY2022 3,127+18, FY2021 3,479+105. A new US$1bn programme runs March 2025 - March 2027 (authorised, not spent).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (filing header 'RMB'million'; ISO CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. Per-share values computed in CNY and converted at CNY/HKD 1.1727 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-16). Parity check on the NYSE ADS (TME, 1 ADS = 2 Class A shares): US$8.655 / 2 x USDHKD 7.8472 = HK$33.96 against the observed HK$34.04 on 1698.HK, a 0.2% tie that confirms the quote basis and the ADS ratio. The USD senior notes (US$500m) are carried at the filing's RMB translation (3,497).
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-03-31 cover-page count, adjusted for the May-2026 Ximalaya issuance
inputs.wacc_rationale: 10.5% for ALL THREE scenarios, built in the flows' own currency (RMB), not from a USD rate: China 10-year government bond ~1.8% + equity risk premium ~6.0% + ~2.7pp China-platform regulatory/geopolitical/VIE premium. This is the same construction and the same rate used on 9999.HK (NetEase), the closest house comparable (RMB flows, HKD quote, cash-rich consumer-internet platform, 20-F filer), so the two are comparable. Risk is charged ONCE: business risk (MAU decline, live-streaming regulation, Ximalaya integration) lives in the probability-weighted scenarios, so no per-scenario WACC differences and no ad-hoc premium stacked on top. A 3.5% nominal RMB terminal growth would be aggressive for China; base uses 2.5%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: the full lease cash payment (principal 124 in financing + ~11 lease interest inside 'payments for interests' 119, of which ~71 is the 2% coupon on US$500m notes) is charged inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path (0.4% of revenue), and lease liabilities (316) are EXCLUDED from net debt. Cash-tax EBIT uses D&A ex right-of-use depreciation: reported D&A 1,375 (4.2% of revenue) less ~130 ROU depreciation = ~1,245 = 3.8%, which is the da_pct_path. Cross-check: FY2025 core operating profit after full D&A (13,364 - interest income 1,054 - other gains 2,632 = 9,678) ties to the component EBIT at FY0 drivers (~9,670).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests charged ONCE, in the bridge: NCI carrying value 2,763 at 2025-12-31 (up from 1,863; 552 arose from a FY2025 business combination with a 379 put-option liability recognised against reserves) is deducted as an equity_bridge item. The flows are consolidated (FY2025 NCI profit share 297 = 2.6% of profit) and are NOT separately reduced for NCI, so there is no double charge. Calibration: component NOPAT at FY0 drivers ~7,800 vs reported attributable profit ex one-offs (11,056 - 2,632 other gains - 1,054 interest income x ~0.85 tax shield + 129 finance costs x 0.85) ~7,650, within non-operating noise.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, scenario-weighted, 10-year component build, per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md routing (operating company, consumer internet; non-US adaptations applied: RMB WACC, CNY->HKD dual currency, leases treatment B, NCI in bridge, matching-asset rule for stripped investment income). No prior model decision in MEMORY.md; fresh build. *** FY0 NORMALISATION *** FY2025 operating profit 13,364 is inflated by interest income 1,054 and other gains 2,632 (of which 2,373 is a one-off gain on deemed disposal of an associate; the rest is dividend income 173, government grants, fair-value changes). Core EBITDA pre-SBC = 13,364 - 1,054 - 2,632 + D&A 1,375 + SBC 669 = 11,722 = 35.6% of revenue, which anchors the margin path; naive EBITDA on reported operating profit would read 44.7%. *** MATCHING-ASSET RULE *** Every stripped income stream has its asset in the bridge: interest income <-> cash and term deposits (net_debt); dividend income, share of associates and the deemed-disposal gain <-> FVOCI investments 26,231 + equity-method investments 1,659 (equity_bridge, at 75% of carrying value). *** HORIZON *** 10 years because the owner-FCF margin is still moving: Ximalaya consolidation dilutes the blended margin in FY2026-27 before the music-mix shift and scale on content costs restore it; base margin flattens from year 7. *** XIMALAYA (post-balance-sheet, closed May 2026) *** Consideration: US$1.26bn cash (~RMB9,010m at ~7.15, deducted in equity_bridge because it left the balance sheet after 2025-12-31) + up to 5.1986% of shares (~153.8m issued at closing) + up to 0.37% founder tranches (~11.6m), both in the share count. Its flows are INCLUDED in the growth path: ~RMB7bn of annual revenue at a materially lower EBITDA margin (mid-teens), consolidated for ~7 months of FY2026 and fully from FY2027 -- that is why FY2026-27 revenue growth is well above the ~5% organic rate (music +10-12% vs social entertainment -5 to -8%) and why the blended margin dips. SAMR conditions (no fee increases, maintained free-content share, no exclusive copyright deals) cap the synergy case. *** SEGMENT MIX *** Online music 26,726 (81%, +22.9%) vs social entertainment 6,176 (19%, -7.3%); the growth path is mid-cycle on the blend, not an extrapolation of FY2025's +15.8%. *** PRICE CONTEXT *** The stock is ~63% below its 52-week high (91.55); Q2-2026 results (Aug-2026) triggered sell-side cuts on slowing membership/ARPPU momentum, ad deceleration and Ximalaya integration cost. The bear case is built to be the path the market is pricing (music growth stalling, blended margins compressing toward the mid-20s, Ximalaya value-destructive), not a mild slowdown. *** BAND *** SBC is small (2% of revenue) so the house/street band is narrow; band_position is reported but the SBC treatment is not the valuation's swing factor -- the net cash, the investment portfolio and the China discount rate are.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +16% = ~5% organic (music +11%, social -7%) + ~7 months of Ximalaya (~RMB4bn); FY2027 +12% = ~5% organic + Ximalaya full-year (~RMB3bn incremental); thereafter organic only, decelerating from 7% to 3% as paying-ratio/ARPPU gains mature against a declining MAU base.
base.margin_note: FY0 core EBITDA pre-SBC 35.6%. Dips to 33.5% on full Ximalaya consolidation at a mid-teens margin, then recovers to 36% as the music mix (gross margin 44.2% in FY2025, up from 42.3%) and scale on content costs outweigh the social-entertainment decline and SAMR fee caps.
base.tax_note: FY2025 cash taxes 1,821 on core pre-tax profit ~9,600 = 19%; the deemed-disposal gain was not taxed. Statutory 25% with HNTE subsidiaries at 15%; the step to 20% adds PRC withholding tax as dividend repatriation grows with the payout.
base.wc_note: Prepaid subscription model: deferred revenue +567 on revenue growth of 4,501 in FY2025 (12.6%); three-year net working-capital inflow 1,309 on 4,563 of revenue growth but dominated by accounts-payable swings (+1,845 FY2024, -783 FY2025). 10% capture on the change in revenue.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: three independent structural pressures (16+ quarters of MAU decline to ByteDance, live-streaming regulation that has already halved social entertainment, and a Tencent-controlled WVR/VIE structure in which minorities cannot stop value-destructive M&A such as a RMB14bn Ximalaya deal with SAMR behavioural conditions), plus the August-2026 sell-side downgrades on slowing membership and ARPPU momentum. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several things to go right together: ARPPU expansion despite fee caps, Ximalaya synergy under no-exclusivity conditions, and an MAU stabilisation that has not happened in four years. Base 50%. Same 25/50/25 split as 9999.HK, the house RMB comparable.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
